existing_answers.what: The Opus refute reviewer names the PR head SHA. A push after review needs a re-read of the diff since that SHA. Per register id, it names the test that fails on base and passes on head, and lists changed expected values, removed assertions and new skips.
Each fail-before line cites the command run on the base SHA and its output, or says 'read, not run'.
Recurring defect shapes go into the reviewer brief, plus 'which copy of new stored state is authoritative'. This aims at state-adding fixes.
The owner reads the invariant-touching hunks on Opus-owned PRs. Verification is tiered by risk, with the full suite before close.
'Do not apply this prescribed fix' entries warn when a diff reintroduces a known-bad fix. This works across time, not inside one round, and is unbuilt.

A regression gate with rollback (measured, function-level), impact-selected tests (TDAD) and fail-before reproduction tests (a sound oracle; its effect on convergence is unmeasured). Round caps are not measured anywhere.

items.residual_gap: What is missing: a stop rule; revert-on-regression in place of patch-on-patch; a per-round record that splits each finding into old-and-open, fix-induced or independent; a blast-radius list for each fix; a rule that a fix which adds state must test every way that state ends; and an independent read of the final fix diff (the root alone is not independent). FixFlow's section 0 already has the reproduction test per register id and the head-SHA binding. It lacks the other five. Nobody has measured whether any of them lowers the fix-induced rate on a real multi-module app.
items.research_question: Under the fix-round contract below, does the rate of fix-induced P1/P2 per fixed P1/P2 fall below the clinic baseline over the next five gated branches? The baseline is at least 15 fix-induced P1/P2 against about 110 fixed, and at least 5 of 19 for P1 alone (my arithmetic on the board's words). First pin the baseline exactly: one Sonnet pass classifies every round-2+ finding in clinic-build task.md as old, fix-induced or independent. Reading cannot settle this, because the only measured evidence comes from function-level benchmarks.

mechanisms.name: Fix-round contract (bounded, with rollback)
mechanisms.what: 1. Each finding gets a reproduction test that fails on the pre-fix commit and passes after; the existing section 0 rule, applied to every P1/P2. 2. The full gate runs before the fix commit (all steps, mypy included; A3-13). If any previously passing test fails, revert the fix commit and retry once; never patch on patch. 3. The re-review is a FRESH refute reviewer, not the root. It is briefed with the fix diff since the verdict SHA, the prior findings list and the blast radius, and labels each finding old, fix-induced or independent. 4. At most two fix rounds. A third, or any fix that touches lines an earlier fix round changed (the pseudo-cycle sign), escalates: revert that fix family and redesign it with an Opus design note, or the owner carries it as a named risk. 5. Stop rule: an independent re-review of the whole fix diff finds no P1/P2 that was not already on the list, and every reproduction test is green. Each merge records 'final head reviewed by: X' (A2-08).
mechanisms.cost: Brief and template text, about an hour. One full check per round (274-840 s on this PC, plus queue waits) and one fresh Opus reviewer per round, much as today. Rounds should fall.
mechanisms.proof: Over the next five gated branches: fix-induced P1/P2 divided by P1/P2 fixed, against the baseline of at least 15/110 (at least 5/19 for P1). Also rounds per branch, and how many branches end root-only. Adopt if the fix-induced P1 count is zero and the overall rate falls below half the baseline.

mechanisms.name: State-exit table for fixes that add a hold, lock, marker or status
mechanisms.what: Before re-review, any fix that adds state lists every way the state can end: post, abandon, reverse, owner or preparer absent, crash mid-write, rollback. Each exit gets one test. Recovery scripts get the full table of record state x marker x serving, with a drill per cell (A2-02, A2-03 transfer).
mechanisms.cost: 30-60 minutes per such fix. Applies only to a minority of fixes.
mechanisms.proof: Retrospective: apply the table to the cutoff-guards and S11 histories and check whether it demands the tests GD-01, RS-1, GV-01 and GV-02 needed (target 4 of 4). Forward: zero 'state never ends or is lost' findings in later rounds.

mechanisms.name: Blast-radius report attached to every fix diff
mechanisms.what: A deterministic list made by script: functions and classes changed, their callers and importers (AST or grep), files co-changed with them in git log, and the test ids that touch them. The reviewer must clear each line. Run those tests first, then the full suite.
mechanisms.cost: A script of about 100-200 lines, no install. It runs in seconds.
mechanisms.proof: For each fix-induced finding in the trial: was its file in the report? Target at least 80% coverage. Compare the regression rate against the trial branches without the report.

thought_structures.why: Only best-of-N with an executable selector has coding evidence (Agentless, CodeMonkeys; B1 C6/C8). Its use on review-fix rounds is unmeasured (B1 C10), and it multiplies checks on a PC that already queues (B07) and tokens toward limits. At most, trial 2-3 candidate fixes chosen by the reproduction test plus the full suite, only for P1 fixes in stateful code. ToT, FoT and LLM-judge trees: no. Repeated LLM review invents defects (B3 C4).

graph_recall.why: Code-structure neighbourhood (callers, importers, co-change) is the blast-radius report. TDAD measured a 70% cut in regressions from it, on small models (B3 C3; B2 C6/C10). A plain script gives it; no graph store is needed. Temporal facts matter only through the knowledge store's 'do not apply' entries.

items.residual_gap: Claims are prose, so no script can resolve them. Four pieces are missing: a typed claims file per slice; a resolver that checks names, paths, hashes and commits; a mutation runner for 'fails without guard' claims; and a place to run all of it that a slice cannot skip. There is also no claims-checked denominator, so nobody knows the real overstatement rate.
items.research_question: No reading is needed. Smallest experiment: in a disposable clone of the clinic repo, replay a resolver over the committed task and review records at each gate's head SHA. It checks that every cited test id is in the collect-only list, every cited path and evidence file exists, and each evidence file's commit matches. The deciding number: does it flag at least half of the recorded overstatements whose class a script can check (name, path or mutation), with under 10 percent false flags on claims the gates accepted?

mechanisms.name: Claims file plus resolver (claimcheck)
mechanisms.what: Each slice commits evidence/claims.json. Each entry has: id, finding id, kind (test_exists, fails_without, passes_on_head, file_has, ran_command), test node id, mutant patch path, evidence path with sha256, and the commit it ran on. A zero-dep Node script checks five things: (1) node ids are in `pytest --collect-only -q` on head; (2) evidence paths exist and hashes match; (3) the evidence commit equals head, or the cited files are unchanged since (git diff --quiet sha..head -- paths); (4) every backticked test_* name in task.md or review prose is in the collected set (this would have caught GE-01 mechanically); (5) ran_command claims match a transcript tool_use with its exit code (G2-F183). Where it runs: first step of the root's gate, before any model reviewer reads (zero tokens). Also as the slice's Stop hook with exit 2, behind a wrapper that fails closed if the script is missing.
mechanisms.cost: About a day to build. Seconds to a few minutes per gate (collect-only runs in the slice's container). Zero model tokens.
mechanisms.proof: Retro replay: share of the 20+ recorded instances flagged, and the false-flag rate. Live, over the next five gates: overstatements that model reviewers find but the resolver missed in a checkable class (target 0), plus review rounds per branch against the gate_rounds table.

mechanisms.name: Mechanical mutation runner for 'fails without guard' claims
mechanisms.what: This is A2-06 run by a script, the same discipline as the knowledge-store design's inject-control. Apply the committed mutant patch in a temporary worktree and run only the named tests. Require the named test to fail with an assertion failure (not an error) and to pass on head. Record 'another guard still catches it' as a redundant-guard finding, not a pass.
mechanisms.cost: Hours to build. One targeted test run per claim, seconds to a minute with the database container.
mechanisms.proof: In replay, the four experiments later found misleading (G06-08, G08-05, G10-23, G05-21) are flagged. Live: zero later findings of the form 'the experiment proves less than claimed'.

verdicts.plain_explanation:
WHAT THE METHODS ARE. Tree of Thoughts has the model write several partial answers, score each, and grow only the promising ones, so it searches a tree instead of following one line. Its measured gain is on puzzles such as Game of 24 (GPT-4: 4% with chain of thought against 74% with ToT), on a 2023 model that does not reason internally. Secondary sources put its cost at roughly 5 to 20 times plain prompting (research.txt B1 C1). Forest of Thought runs several such trees at once and settles on an answer by consensus and self-correction. Only its abstract could be read: it gives no benchmark, model, number or cost, so it is an unverified claim aimed at math and logic (B1 C3). Graph of Thoughts treats each partial answer as a node that can be merged with others, refined in a loop, or distilled. It was measured only on toy tasks like sorting (62% better than ToT at 31% less cost than ToT), never on merging code or agents' work (B1 C2, C11).

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES FOR CODE. (1) At matched compute, plain self-consistency (sample several answers, take the majority) often equals or beats the elaborate structures. Debate and Reflexion can get worse as the budget grows (B1 C4; math and QA only). (2) The only family with software evidence is best-of-n patch sampling with test-based selection. Agentless on SWE-bench Lite: majority vote alone resolved 25.67%, adding a regression-test filter 27.0%, adding a generated reproduction-test filter 32.0%. That took 40 candidates per issue at about 78k tokens per issue. Only 94 of 213 reproduction tests were valid, and the best possible pick over the candidates was 42%, so the selector is the weak link (B1 C6, C8). (3) Iterative review-and-fix loops damage working code faster than they repair broken code, and they fall into cycles of adding and removing the same change. A verification gate (rerun the earlier tests, roll back on failure, retry) was the only strategy that helped every model in an 8-turn study (B1 C9; B3 C4, C5; function-level benchmarks, older models). (4) No study measures the exact idea here: N candidate fixes per review finding, chosen by executed tests, with regression as the outcome (B1 C10, unsupported). (5) No controlled study re-tests ToT on 2025-2026 reasoning models (B1 C5, could not check).

WHAT THE TESTBED SHOWS. The selector in the testbed's gate was always a model reading code. The round-2 reviewer 'ran no tests, scripts or database commands' (opening-cutoff-guards/evidence/review-opus-round2.md:3, confirmed in the file). Nine of the eleven slice gates S00 to S10 took three rounds (A2-01). In round 2 or later, a fix produced a new P1 or P2 on 8 of about 20 gated branches: S01, S02, S06, S07, the cutoff guards, S11, the posting follow-ups and the faster check. That includes five fix-induced P1s: W1 in S07 (task.md:258, confirmed), GD-01 and RS-1 in the cutoff guards (task.md:631, confirmed; opening-cutoff-guards/task.md:83), and GV-01 and GV-02 in S11 (A2-02, A2-03, A2-04, the fix_induced table in sweep-tables.txt). The board never consistently splits a round's findings into still open, caused by the fix, and new but independent (A2-04 limits). So no per-finding fix-induced rate exists, only these counts. Nothing converged on a rule. The build stopped on the owner's USER-24 direction (task.md:786, confirmed; A2-10). The failures were state and ordering bugs: a hold that never ends, a recovery boundary lost after a rollback. Only a test written for that invariant catches them. A tree is only as good as that test.

WHAT FRONTIER MODELS ALREADY DO, AND WHAT AN OUTER STRUCTURE STILL ADDS. Opus- and Sonnet-class models with extended thinking already branch, check and backtrack inside one call. So a prompt-level ToT, FoT or GoT, where the model proposes, scores and expands thoughts as text, repeats work the model does internally, at several times the tokens. Its scorer is a model judging its own thoughts, which is the overstating problem (B12) again. That redundancy is reasoned, not measured (B1 C5). An outer structure still adds three things the model cannot give itself. (a) An executable verifier: the model cannot run the test suite inside its thinking, and executed tests were the part of Agentless that carried the gain. (b) Isolation: candidates written in separate worktrees or contexts do not anchor on each other's first idea. They are still one model, so their errors stay correlated. (c) Parallel wall-clock: on this PC the gain is capped by the check queue (B06 to B08) and the usage limit (B03). The outer structure worth testing is therefore not ToT, FoT or GoT. It is best-of-n with an executed, pre-written selector, used in one narrow place.

ALREADY COVERED ELSEWHERE. Fail-before and pass-after per finding is already the ship plan's reviewer rule (ship-plan-section0.md: the reviewer names the test that fails on base and passes on head) plus Horthy G2-F015. The token tally the trial needs is Horthy G2-F183 (trial 2), and the transcript-forensics script shape is in card CR-03. The paired, blind, pre-registered design follows Horthy trial 1 (G4-F034).

where_it_helps.place: The slice's fix step for each round-1 P1 or P2 on money, stock, hold or lock, state-machine, or deploy/restore code: several candidate fixes per finding, in separate worktrees or contexts
where_it_helps.bottleneck: B01 (fix rounds that create new defects); also B17 (all review is model reading)
where_it_helps.mechanism: The tree is made of K=3 candidate fixes for one finding, written independently from the same brief, with no candidate seeing another. The selector is executed, not a model. First, a reproduction test for the finding, plus a 'how does this state end' test for any new hold or lock (the A2-02 transfer), written once BEFORE any candidate and frozen. Each candidate must make it pass, and it must fail on the base commit. Second, the tests of the touched app plus the serial race tests, run in the Linux container. Third, a guard-removal check: delete the candidate's new guard, and the frozen test must fail (the A2-06 lock-removal idea, made mechanical). Ties go to the smallest diff by files touched. A model reviewer then reads only the winner, as today.
where_it_helps.evidence: Measured but indirect. Agentless: test filters raised SWE-bench Lite resolves from 25.67% to 32.0% over majority vote. The pick recovered 96 of the 126 issues where some candidate was right, and most of the gain came from the reproduction test (B1 C6). A verification gate with rollback was the only strategy that cut regressions for every model in an 8-turn study (B1 C9). Unmeasured: whether this lowers fix-induced P1s and P2s in review-driven rounds (B1 C10 unsupported). The selector's weak point is measured too: generated reproduction tests were valid in only 94 of 213 cases (B1 C6), and plausible-but-wrong patches pass tests (B3 C1: 7.8% and 29.6%). That is why the test is written and frozen before the candidates and checked by guard removal. In the testbed, model-run lock-removal experiments were later found to prove less than claimed at least four times (A2-06), so the guard removal must be scripted, not reported.
where_it_helps.cost: About 3x the fix-phase tokens for each finding the method covers. November per-slice tokens were never measured (critic coverage gap), so the real multiple must come from a transcript tally. Checks: K narrow runs per finding instead of one. The full 7-step check (274 to 726 s whole, A2 root_check_per_merge) still runs once, on the winner only. Recorded second-slot waits were 337 to 551 s (sweep-tables A3 slot pairs), so K full checks per finding would land directly in the queue.

where_it_helps.place: The reviewer's verdict on a fix (the B12 side of the same mechanism)
where_it_helps.mechanism: There is no tree here. The by-product of the trial above: because the selector is a script that executes a frozen test and a guard removal, the claim 'the test proves the fix' is checked by running it, not by another model reading the record. That is the transfer A2-05 asks for (a resolvable test id that fails with the guard removed).
where_it_helps.evidence: At least 20 overstatement records in the testbed, with no denominator, so no rate (A2-05). Wrong-but-passing patch rates are measured on SWE-bench (B3 C1). Lane B1 itself says this mechanical rerun is supported and model-judge or debate verification is not (B1 implications, B12).
where_it_helps.cost: Small: one script per finding, run inside the narrow test scope above.

where_it_does_not.place: B03 usage limit: any tree, forest or graph run as a standing practice
where_it_does_not.why: These methods multiply calls. Agentless used 40 candidates per issue, and CodeMonkeys cost about $2,300 for one SWE-bench Verified run (B1 C6, C8, B03 implication). The testbed's own measurement: subagents made 82.4% of calls and caused 91 of the 104 limit errors, and one window carried only about 3.4M subagent tokens (CR-03, CR-04). A standing K-way fan-out on every finding would make the 6 November stoppage come sooner.

where_it_does_not.place: B06, B07, B08 check queue and memory: one full check per candidate
where_it_does_not.why: The whole check is 274 to 726 s on merged main (A2 root_check_per_merge). The second slot opens only with 8 GiB free (check.py:80, A3 constants), and recorded second-slot waits are 337 to 551 s, the largest single wait 742 s (critic). K full checks per finding put the cost exactly where the PC is already short. Candidates may only run narrow tests, and one at a time if memory is low.

where_it_does_not.place: B12 and B17: a model judge or debate as the value function (ToT and MCTS-style scoring, SWE-Search's value agent)
where_it_does_not.why: The overstating problem is the selector. LLM critics claim bugs in bug-free code, and repair rate trails damage rate (B1 C9, B3 C4). Debate and Reflexion can degrade as the budget grows (B1 C4). SWE-Search's gains are self-reported and relative, with no equal-cost comparison (B1 C7). A model scoring model-written branches adds a second layer of unverified claims.

where_it_does_not.place: A forest of reviewers with majority vote on findings (self-consistency applied to review)
where_it_does_not.why: Voting would throw away real defects. In one small study, 56.5% of confirmed defects were found by exactly one model, and adding a second vendor raised coverage from 33.6% to 57.1% (B3 C9, Stone; small and not peer reviewed). Several independent reviewers help through their union, not through consensus. The testbed's two refute-reviewers, split by area (A2-01), already take the union.

where_it_does_not.place: B04 single orchestrator, and GoT as an orchestration architecture
where_it_does_not.why: The structured-reasoning papers are about one problem's answer, not about throughput (B1 B04 implication). The orchestrator's measured problem is context size (3 compactions at 573,774 to 974,246 pre-tokens, CR-05) and serial merging. A graph of thoughts adds more for it to hold. The transferable fragment, bounded distillation of parallel outputs (Parallel-Distill-Refine, math only), is just short structured verdicts, which the harness already demands (orchestration-design.md output contracts).

where_it_does_not.place: B13 shared-document edits merged by GoT-style aggregation
where_it_does_not.why: GoT aggregation was measured only on sorting-type tasks. No source shows it merging agents' documents (B1 C11). The testbed's measured failure was the root's own merge edits breaking the check (A2-07: S01 two failures, S02 four consequences). The answer there is per-slice append-only fragments and lock-step tests, not a model merging text.

where_it_does_not.place: B02 gaps found only at the end, and B19 nothing run on a real host
where_it_does_not.why: A search over candidates cannot find what was never tested. The missing check was a clean-install journey with real-shaped data (A2-13). FeatureBench shows unit-level success does not predict feature-level success (B3 C10: 11.0% against 74.4%). That calls for an acceptance test, not a reasoning method.

where_it_does_not.place: Candidate designs for new holds, locks or recovery rules (a tree over designs before code)
where_it_does_not.why: The scorer would be a model judge, because there is no executable test of a design yet. The testbed's lesson points to a cheaper deterministic tool: enumerate the state table (record state x marker x serving; post, abandon, reverse, owner absent) and drill every cell (A2-02, A2-03 transfers). That checklist does the work a design tree would claim to do, with no extra branches.

These are machine, ops, visibility, housekeeping, platform-parity, load-test and backlog-policy problems. No thought structure bears on them; each needs an engineering fix or an owner policy (lanes B3 to B6).

trial.design: One slice, an A/B within that slice, chosen before the gate runs: the next slice whose round-1 gate returns at least 4 P1 or P2 findings on money, stock, hold or lock, state-machine, or deploy/restore code. Assign each finding by a coin flip recorded in the decisions journal before any fixing. CONTROL arm: today's procedure, one fix per finding by the slice session, then the targeted Opus re-review. CANDIDATE arm, for each finding: (1) a separate Opus agent writes the reproduction test (fails on base, plus a 'how does this state end' test if the fix adds a hold or lock). It is committed and frozen, and its sha256 is recorded before any candidate exists (the answer-key discipline of Horthy G2-F051). (2) K=3 candidate fixes, each an Opus agent in its own worktree with the same brief and no view of the others. Routing puts money and state code on Opus. (3) A script selects: the frozen test must fail on base and pass on the candidate; the touched app's tests and the serial race tests must pass in the Linux container; removing the candidate's new guard must make the frozen test fail. Ties go to the fewest files touched. If no candidate passes, that counts as a failed round, and that finding falls back to the control procedure. (4) Only the winner goes to the same blind targeted Opus re-review as the control. The reviewer is not told which arm a fix came from. No model judge selects anywhere. Nothing goes into the harness unless the stop rule's pass condition is met.
trial.measurement: Primary: new P1 and P2 findings per fix round that are CAUSED BY THE FIX, per arm. Each re-review finding is classified, by a second blind Opus pass and checked by the root, as (a) old and still open, (b) new and caused by the fix, or (c) new and independent. This is the split card A2-04 says the board never kept. Testbed reference baseline, approximate only because the board did not split consistently: fix-induced P1s or P2s appeared in round 2 or later on 8 of about 20 gated branches, including five fix-induced P1s (W1, GD-01, RS-1, GV-01, GV-02), against 19 round-1 P1s on 12 branches (sweep-tables A2). Secondary: (a) rounds until the finding is closed; (b) how often the winner was candidate 1. If it almost always is, selection adds nothing over one fix; (c) how often the frozen test was found wrong or weak, since that is the selector's failure rate; (d) fix-phase tokens per finding per arm, from a transcript tally over the session JSONL (Horthy G2-F183, CR-03 script shape); (e) narrow-run count, check-minutes and slot waits per arm, from the check's own logs.
trial.budget: At most 6 findings in the candidate arm, so at most 18 candidate fixes and 6 frozen tests. Fix-phase tokens in the candidate arm capped at 3.5x the control arm's mean per finding. Measure the control arm first. If November per-slice figures are still unmeasured, set the cap after the first two control findings. No candidate work starts within the last 90 minutes of a 5-hour window, nor once the weekly meter is above an owner-set level, because the limit typically hit about 75 minutes into the window in October (CR-03). Checks: candidates run only narrow scope (frozen test, touched-app tests, serial race tests) in the Linux container. The full 7-step check runs once per arm per round, on the selected fix only, never per candidate. Candidate narrow runs run one at a time when free memory is below 8 GiB, matching the existing slot rule (check.py:80).
trial.stop_rule: Pre-registered. Stop early and record 'do not adopt' if any of these happen: (1) the candidate arm's token use passes the cap on two findings; (2) the winner is candidate 1 in at least 3 of the first 4 findings, so selection adds nothing; (3) the frozen test is found wrong or too weak (passes with the guard removed, or the reviewer shows it tests the wrong invariant) on 2 findings, so the selector cannot be trusted; (4) a usage-limit stop or a slot wait over 742 s, the largest recorded, is caused by candidate runs. Otherwise stop after 6 candidate-arm findings, or when the slice's gate closes if sooner. Adopt as an opt-in for P1 findings on money, state and recovery code only, never as a default, if the candidate arm had zero fix-induced P1s and at least 2 fewer fix-induced P1 plus P2 findings than the control arm. With this sample that is a weak signal, so the result is an option for a second slice, not a rule. Any smaller difference counts as no effect. If the trial does not pass, keep the cheaper part it tests on its own: the frozen fail-before test plus the scripted guard removal, single fix.

do_not_build: A prompt-level Tree of Thoughts, Forest of Thought or Graph of Thoughts layer in briefs or agents (propose, score, expand thoughts as text). Frontier models already search inside extended thinking; the measured gains are on puzzles with a 2023 model at 5 to 20x cost.

Any MCTS or tree-search coding agent with a model judge as its value function (the SWE-Search or CodeTree pattern). The gains are self-reported and relative, with no equal-cost comparison, and the judge is the overstating problem.
Majority vote or consensus over reviewers' findings. Single-reviewer finds are most of the real defects, so keep the union.
Multi-agent debate or Reflexion loops as a reviewer or fixer. At matched compute they are no better than self-consistency and can degrade as budget grows.
GoT-style model aggregation for merging slice outputs or shared documents. Use per-slice append-only fragments, mechanical merges and lock-step drift tests instead.
A standing K-way candidate fan-out on every finding, or any candidate run that triggers a full 7-step check per candidate.
More model-review rounds as the cure for B01. Iterative LLM review invents defects and cycles; the measured mitigation is a test gate with rollback, plus a pre-registered stopping rule.
open_research: Whether ToT- or FoT-style prompting adds anything on 2025-2026 reasoning models at equal budget. No controlled study was found in two searches (B1 C5), so the 'redundant' judgment is reasoned, not measured.

Whether N candidate fixes per review finding, picked by executed tests, cut fix-induced regressions compared with one fix per round. No study measures it (B1 C10). Only the in-house trial above can answer it for this kind of code.

The fix-induced defect rate per finding in the testbed itself. A re-read of the S01 to S11 gate records, classifying each round-2 and later finding as still-open, caused-by-fix or independent, would give the trial a real baseline instead of branch counts. It is cheap, read-only work over docs/tasks.

November per-slice token use and limit hits. The root transcript 7f348b2c and the slice transcripts were never analysed (critic coverage gap). Rerunning the CR-03 forensics script shape on them is a prerequisite for any token cap.

How long a narrow test run (one app's tests plus the serial race tests) takes in the Linux container. Only whole-check and pass-level timings were measured (parallel pass alone 171 s; serial pass about 104 to 160 s), so the trial's check-minute cost is estimated, not known.
Full texts of Forest-of-Thought, SWE-Search, CodeTree, CodeMonkeys and the two 2026 regression papers. Only abstracts were read, so model lists and most effect sizes are missing.
Whether a different-family candidate writer or reviewer reduces correlated errors among candidates. Two small studies conflict (B3 C9).

verdicts.question: Could spatial and temporal topology in recall from graphs boost token efficiency for this harness, and does the testbed already hold "a SQLite graph-based library for a self-evolving repository"?
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Partly, and mostly not through a graph. The tokens went into the root's large resident window (592.7M cache-read tokens over 1,107 calls) and into reports and diffs passing through it. A small SQLite store of what is valid now (slice status, gate verdicts, open findings, decisions), written only by deterministic tools, could let the root run with a small window. A recursive "neighbourhood of this fix" query is a cheap add-on, worth having only if a zero-token replay shows it finds where the fix-induced defects landed. No such library exists in the testbed, and none of the testbed's own trials measured a token gain.
verdicts.plain_explanation:
WHAT EXISTS. The testbed holds no SQLite graph library and nothing self-evolving (sweep-critic.txt "Confirmed not found"; I confirmed that .claude holds only worktrees/ and that 09-operational/runs/ is empty). It has four near things:
- The corpus map. It is a typed-edge graph of 11 planning files, stored as JSONL rather than SQLite (A6-04). Its validation contract was never run (A6-10).
- The context system. It is compaction steering plus exact grep recall (A5-01, A5-02) and was never installed. Its only token results are increases: +10.31 % (A5-11) and +6.08 % over a plain notes file, +17.02 % over native (A5-13; RESULTS_2026-10-15.md:13-15,22 checked).
- The root's lesson memory (CR-01): 15 markdown files outside git.
- In the other repository, the unbuilt knowledge-store design. It is the likeliest source of the owner's memory (critic, on A5-03).

TERMS FOR THIS HARNESS.
- "Spatial" means the neighbourhood of a thing. In the code: files, symbols, imports, callers, files changed together. In the work: slices, branches and the dependencies between slices.
- "Temporal" means two times for each fact. Valid time is when it was true, keyed to code state: valid from a commit until it is superseded or invalidated. Recorded time is when the harness wrote it: journal sequence and git history.

(a) WHERE THE TOKENS WENT. These are my own read-only tallies of the root transcript 7f348b2c, made today. Character counts undercount tokens by about 25-35 % (CR-03 r1-26).
- The root's resident window is the main sink. There were 1,107 calls, with 592.7M cache-read, 14.6M cache-write and 1.8M output tokens, a mean of about 549k tokens resident per call. Compactions came at 573,774, 974,246 and 967,210 tokens, plus a fourth on 11 Nov 00:49Z at 969,988 (CR-05 counted three). They dropped 3,393,198 tokens in total and each paused 101-125 s.
- The root's 72 subagent files made 2,393 calls but only 331.7M cache reads. So in November the root itself, not its subagents, spent most tokens. This reverses October's 82 % subagent share of calls (CR-03). Slice sessions are still unmeasured.
- The root's incoming material totalled 3.34M characters of tool results:
  - git diff/show: 943k (222 calls)
  - other file reads: 831k
  - the board: 118 read/grep calls, 187k, plus 170k from other task.md reads. The board is now 838 lines and 221,112 bytes.
  - git log: 179k
  - session event lists: 239k
- On top of that came 722k characters of task notifications (115 messages). Reports in total were about 1.1M characters, roughly a quarter of what the root took in.
- Fixed cost per session is about 70k tokens of tool and MCP schemas, plus 8.7k-34.7k of mandatory pre-reading (CR-11).

Which kind of recall would cut each sink:
- Recall by time cuts the board reread and the resident window, but only as an enabler. The saving comes from a small window, and the store is what lets the root shrink without losing state.
- Recall by neighbourhood cuts only the pre-read routing and reviewer localisation.
- Neither cuts reports. Output contracts and files cut those. Subagents can write files (machine-facts.md, B16).
- The outside evidence for "retrieval saves tokens" is retrieval against FULL context: Zep 115k to 1.6k (B2 C1), Mem0 26k to 1.8k at lower accuracy (C2). Graph against a flat indexed table is not shown, and a filesystem agent matched graph memory (C3).
- Deterministic code graphs have a measured localisation gain: about +4 points Acc@5 over strong agents at equal cost (LocAgent, C6), and +4.9 from history (RepoMem, C10). But repos under 10k commits lost 13.1 points, and the testbed has 442 commits.

(b) WHAT THE KNOWLEDGE-STORE DESIGN ALREADY HAS (refs/knowledge-store-design.md §3-5).
- An append-only journal of events in git as truth (recorded time), and a SQLite index that is rebuilt from it, never migrated (§3.1).
- Footprints: typed items such as file blobs, config keys, dependency versions and preconditions (§3.5).
- Validity by code state, invalidated by events and never by age (§5.1, §5.2). This is bi-temporal in substance.
- Lineage through one recursive CTE over entry_link (§3.7).
- A spatial check by identifier, ks lookup --diff (§3.7, §5.2).
- Questions about a past state, answered by folding a journal commit (§5.6).
- Token columns on every lookup (§3.6).

What it lacks:
- Orchestrator state: slice, branch, status, gate round, verdict, finding with severity and file:line, decision with supersession, and dependencies between slices.
- Any import, caller or co-change neighbourhood. Symbol spans are deferred to KS-6b. Graphify was skipped (harness-review.md §5); dependency-cruiser was adopted only as import rules.
- So it cannot answer "what does this fix's blast radius touch, and which open findings and active branches sit there".

(c) THE SMALLEST THING THAT WOULD CUT TOKENS. Build one SQLite file through node:sqlite, using the knowledge store's journal-then-index pattern, as a sibling that does not wait on the knowledge-store pilot.

Tables:
- event(seq, at, commit_sha, actor, kind, payload): append-only.
- slice(id, branch, status) and slice_dep(slice, needs).
- gate_round(id, slice, round, head_sha, verdict).
- finding(id, gate_round, severity, path, line, status, opened_sha, closed_sha, superseded_by).
- decision(id, text, valid_from_sha, superseded_by, superseded_at_sha), with FTS5 over the text.
- file_edge(src, dst, kind = import or co-change, weight, at_sha).
- commit_file(sha, path).

Queries:
1. Now-state: unmerged slices, last verdict, open P1/P2 counts. About 1-2k tokens replace the board.
2. Decisions still valid on a topic: FTS5 where superseded_at is null.
3. Blast radius: changed paths, then reverse imports to depth 2 by WITH RECURSIVE, plus the top co-changed files. Return those files, the open findings on them, and the active branches touching them.
4. As-of a commit, for replay and audit.
5. Open P3s whose file changed since they were opened, flagged for recheck and never auto-closed (B21).

Who writes:
- Only deterministic tools: git, a Python ast import pass, the check's exit records, and gate verdict JSON returned under a schema. File:line is checked mechanically before the write (BAML T-08). The board becomes a generated view (B13).
- A model never extracts facts from prose.

Who reads: the root at every gate, slice leads at start, and the fix-round reviewer through query 3.

SQLite with recursive CTEs is enough. The scale is tens of slices, hundreds of findings and thousands of edges, and the knowledge store already measured its own CTE choice (E-08). No graph engine is needed.

(d) The deciding measurement is in the trial field.

(e) What not to build, and why, is in do_not_build.

(f) "SELF-EVOLVING", HONESTLY. It can mean four things:
1. Entries are written at solve time by the solving session, with footprints.
2. Entries are invalidated by code change, never by age.
3. A recurring lesson is promoted into a deterministic check (a lint rule or test) after an Opus or owner approval. Horthy adopt 1 (G1-F010, G1-F011, G4-F008) is exactly this shape. CR-01 lessons should flow the same way.
4. Hit and miss counters decide what is kept.

It cannot mean any of these:
- A repository that rewrites its own code or rules unsupervised.
- Learning from prose.
- Knowing that an entry is still correct when nothing in its footprint changed (§5.5).
- Improving the models.
- Any gain that is not measured.

The testbed has only item 1 in a weak form (CR-01, A5-17).

where_it_helps.place: The root orchestrator's resident window (the B04 overflow and compactions)
where_it_helps.mechanism: Recall by time is the enabler; a small window is the saving. A now-state query (open slices, last verdicts, open P1/P2, valid decisions) lets the root be compacted early or restarted fresh per gate without carrying history. A5-07's autoCompactWindow lever then becomes safe to use.
where_it_helps.evidence: Measured today from transcript 7f348b2c: 1,107 calls, 592.7M cache-read tokens, about 549k resident per call, and 4 compactions (573,774; 974,246; 967,210; 969,988, the last on 11 Nov) dropping 3.39M tokens with pauses of 101-125 s. The token saving itself is unmeasured. Outside evidence is only retrieval against full context (Zep 115k to 1.6k, B2 C1). In the testbed a 3 KiB maintained notes file matched a restore adapter and the adapter cost +6 to +17 % (A5-13), so a plain generated state view may capture most of the gain.
where_it_helps.cost: About 300-500 lines of Node using node:sqlite (built in) plus a deterministic loader from git and verdict JSON. No install. A day or two of one session, after the trial says go.

where_it_helps.place: The board reread (829 lines in the sweep, 838 lines and 221,112 bytes today)
where_it_helps.mechanism: Recall by time: serve only facts valid now. Recall by work-neighbourhood: serve only the rows of this slice and the slices it depends on. The board becomes a generated view and is no longer a hand-edited source.
where_it_helps.evidence: Measured today: 118 root board read/grep calls returned 186,593 characters, and 32 other task.md reads returned 170,092, about 11 % of root tool-result characters. Each read then stays resident for later calls. There is no measured test of a smaller view. A7-03 measured a hand-built packet at 20.6 % fewer bytes on synthetic fixtures, and A7-06 found no time gain in a real-agent trial.
where_it_helps.cost: Part of the same store. It also needs the gate's verdict to be returned as schema JSON (orchestration-design output contracts).

where_it_helps.place: Fix rounds: blast radius of a fix (where new P1s came from)
where_it_helps.mechanism: Recall by code-neighbourhood, deterministic: take the changed paths, add reverse imports to depth 2 and the top co-changed files, and list the open findings and active branches on those files. The result is a checklist attached to the reviewer brief. It is never a verdict.
where_it_helps.evidence: Outside: deterministic code graphs give about +4 points Acc@5 over strong agentic baselines at equal cost (LocAgent, B2 C6), and history adds +4.9 (RepoMem, C10). But repos under 10k commits lost 13.1 points, and the testbed has 442 commits. No study measures fewer fix-induced defects. Testbed shape: 9 recorded fix-induced cases (sweep-tables A2, e.g. cutoff guards GC-01 to RR-1..3 to GD-01; S07 W1; S01 V1/V2), and S09 round 2 found the same exposure on S07's pages. That cross-slice neighbourhood case is exactly what this query targets. Its value is unproven.
where_it_helps.cost: An ast import pass for Python/Django in seconds per repo (LocAgent reports seconds), a git log co-change count, and one WITH RECURSIVE query. Zero model tokens to build.

where_it_helps.mechanism: Recall by work-neighbourhood: route the pre-read to the docs and decisions linked to the files and slices this session touches.
where_it_helps.evidence: CR-11: pre-read is 8,753 to 34,749 tokens on top of about 70k of fixed overhead, half of it tool and MCP schemas. Only the pre-read part can shrink, so the ceiling is roughly 10-30 % of a session's starting context. The testbed's contract to test routed reading against the map (A6-10) was never run.
where_it_helps.cost: One more query on the same store. Low value; do it only if the store exists anyway.

where_it_does_not.place: Subagent and session reports passing through the root
where_it_does_not.why: Measured today: 115 task notifications carried 722,157 characters, plus 238,787 from session event lists and 115,002 from Agent results, roughly a quarter of the root's input. Recall does not shorten what a report says. What cuts this is an output contract: the subagent writes its full report to a file and returns verdict fields only. Subagents can write files (machine-facts.md B16; research B5 C9 contradicted the premise). The store helps only as the place the verdict JSON lands.

git diff/show returned 943,260 characters in 222 root calls, 28 % of root tool results. Reading the diff is the gate's job (A1-01). A neighbourhood list can focus a reviewer but cannot replace reading the change. Moving diff reading to a reviewer agent that returns schema output is the lever, and that is an orchestration choice, not recall.
CR-11: tool and MCP schemas, skills, system prompt and memory. Recall does not touch it; trimming tools per agent type does.

where_it_does_not.place: Subagents exploring code with a current frontier model
where_it_does_not.why: The localisation gains were measured with 2024-era models on Python SWE-bench (B2 C6, C10). Vendor claims of about 99 % token cuts were contradicted, and one A/B run had the graph arm using more tokens (C9). Claude Code's own team dropped indexes for agentic search but admits the evidence was 'vibes' (C11). The testbed's Graphify arm was built and never queried (A6-13). There is no basis to expect token savings here.

where_it_does_not.place: A young repository's history (temporal recall from git)
where_it_does_not.why: RepoMem lost 13.1 points on repos with under 10k commits (B2 C10). The testbed has 442 commits since 1 Oct 2026. Co-change edges will be sparse and noisy at first; keep them as a ranked hint only.

where_it_does_not.place: B02 clean-install gaps, B05 to B11 machine issues, B12 overstated reports, B17 to B20 verification
where_it_does_not.why: These are acceptance-test, machine and evidence problems. A graph would not have found the missing seeder step (B2 implications for B02). Overstated reports are fixed by recording facts from deterministic tool output and checking file:line mechanically, not by recall.

trial.design:
Replay recorded gates. Work in a disposable clone of the testbed made outside its folder (the testbed stays read-only).

Stage 0, zero tokens:
- Build file_edge from the clone (Python ast imports plus git co-change).
- For each of the 9 recorded fix-induced defects (sweep-tables A2), plus S09 round 2's exposure on S07's pages, run the blast-radius query on the earlier fix commit.
- Record whether the files of the later defect's fix fall inside the result, and how big the result is.

Stage 1, paired arms:
- Pick 10 gate rounds from the A2 gate-rounds table. Cover early (S01, S02), middle (S05, S07, S10) and late (cutoff guards, S11), and include at least 4 rounds where a fix-induced defect appeared.
- Arm A (without): a fresh Opus gate agent at the recorded head SHA, given the board as it was at that commit and git. This is what the root used.
- Arm B (with): the same model, effort and brief, with the board removed and replaced by the store's queries: now-state, valid decisions and finding lookup, plus the blast-radius query only if stage 0 passed.
- The store is built for each round by the deterministic loader from git and from the board's finding tables at that commit. Where a table does not parse, its rows are hand-entered once as a fixture, frozen and sha256-hashed before any run.
- Two repeats per arm per round, on the same Claude Code build.
- Separately, compute arm A's real-world baseline from the recorded root transcript: tokens between each gate's start and its verdict, flagged as confounded by concurrent work.
trial.measurement:
For each run:
- Root-side tokens: input plus cache-read plus cache-write plus output, from transcript usage fields, not chars/4.
- Tool calls and wall time.
- Recall of the round's recorded P1/P2 findings, scored mechanically by finding id and path against the frozen record.
- For the rounds with a fix-induced defect, whether the arm flagged the area where the next round's defect landed.

For stage 0: the share of the 10 cases whose later-defect files sit inside the depth-2 neighbourhood, and the median neighbourhood size in files.

Report medians per arm with every attempt kept, including usage-limit interruptions recorded separately (A7-07 practice).
trial.budget:
Stage 0: zero model tokens, under an hour of Node.

Stage 1: 40 Opus gate-agent runs (10 rounds x 2 arms x 2 repeats). Cap total spend at an owner-set token figure fixed before launch (the testbed's own practice, A5-15). Run lanes two at a time, with state on disk and no reliance on run-cache resume (CR-04).

Build cost of the loader and queries: about one session.

No installs, no graph engine, no embeddings.
trial.stop_rule:
Stage 0:
- If the neighbourhood contains the later defect's files in fewer than 6 of 10 cases, or the median result exceeds about 15 files, drop the blast-radius query and keep the store flat.

Stage 1:
- Adopt the store only if arm B's median root-side tokens per gate are at least 30 % below arm A's.
- It must also lose no recorded P1 that arm A found, and have equal or better P2 recall.
- If tokens fall but any P1 is lost, the result is 'not adopted': fewer tokens with a missing prerequisite is not a win (A6-10's rule).
- If neither arm finishes cleanly within the cap, the verdict is 'inconclusive, use the simpler workflow': a generated markdown state file plus an earlier compaction setting. The testbed itself showed a plain notes file matching heavier machinery (A5-13).
- Pre-register these labels before launch.

do_not_build: An LLM-extracted knowledge graph of the docs or the code (GraphRAG, Graphiti-style ingestion, Graphify's LLM pass on docs). Extraction costs about 1000x vector indexing (B2 C4, LazyGraphRAG). Graph RAG often underperforms plain RAG (GraphRAG-Bench). Model-extracted edges add errors, which is the B12 overstatement problem in a new place. The testbed's attestation-only map recovered the human-visible chain at no level and 61 % of its labels were singletons (A6-08).

A graph database server (Neo4j-class) or Kuzu. The PC is memory-limited, with free memory often 2-6 GB (B08). Kuzu's repo was archived in Oct 2025 (B2 C12). At tens of slices and thousands of edges, SQLite WITH RECURSIVE answers every query named here.

Embeddings or a vector index (sqlite-vec is pre-v1, C12). The knowledge-store design already found no evidence either way at this scale and gated vectors behind a measured miss trigger (§4.4, D16). Orchestrator facts are ids, paths and statuses, which exact and FTS5 lookups serve.

A memory layer that pushes context into sessions automatically, through hooks or injection. The store is pull-only, as the knowledge-store design rules. Hooks and the context system were deliberately skipped (harness-review.md).
Self-modifying rules or code driven by the store. Promotion of a lesson into a check stays an approved, reviewed change.
Time-to-live or age-based expiry. Invalidate by code change and supersession only (§5.1). The testbed's own context-system work ruled out time-based expiry after it refused valid snapshots (A5-05).
A separate code-graph tool trial before stage 0. Harness-review §5 already skipped Graphify on staleness and package-age grounds.
open_research: Per-slice token use in November. The 18 worktree-session transcripts and the other root-level sessions are unmeasured (critic coverage gaps). Run the CR-03 forensics script shape over them before sizing anything. It costs zero tokens.
Whether the board's findings tables parse deterministically at each historical commit, or how many rows would need hand-entered fixtures for the replay.

Whether a smaller root window alone (autoCompactWindow about 400k, A5-07) gives most of the saving with no store at all. It is version-specific; re-verify on the current Claude Code. The harness review found the setting is keyed per model id under modelSettings.
What each compaction summary lost in the root transcript. Only counts and timings are known (CR-05).
How plan limits count cache-read tokens against the five-hour window (CR-03 r1-23, unknown). This decides whether a cut in resident window size eases B03 stops or only cost.
Co-change quality in a repository with a few hundred commits. No measured study of co-change mining for coding agents was found (B2 C10).
Whether a current frontier reviewer given a blast-radius list catches more fix-induced defects than one without. Nobody has measured regressions per fix round.

attacks.evidence: The reattribution stands. My grep of every clinic transcript found no records at all after hour 09Z on 6 Nov (last hour 2026-11-06T09, 58 records). B5 C6 says scheduled-task prompts 'cannot act as approval or consent'. B5 C1 says auto-continue stops after three continuations and needs Enter after more than 30 min asleep. The root's recap says it waited '34 minutes ... behind the resumed sessions' checks'. Releasing every parked session at once after a restart is a thundering herd on the check queue.

Do not run workflows from a scheduled-task session if they must pause at limits. Add to the recovery chain a staggered resume: at most two sessions released at a time, each after the previous one's check has started (2030 s wait measured when all resumed together).

The testbed's own measurement went the other way: heavier recall cost +6 to +17% over a plain notes file (A5-13). The local merge queue is inference (B6 C3 could_not_check). Gate-as-workflow fans out about 3 agents per slice, and CR-04 measured 10 parallel lanes dying in 15 minutes. How cache-read tokens count against the limit is unknown (CR-03 r1-23). So token cuts may not ease B03 at all.

The larger sink is slice-session windows, which call for one phase per session and an earlier compaction in the slices, not a store. Rate graph recall 'narrow': a generated short board first.
